## Software requirements

```{r lib, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#Data containers
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SingleCellExperiment)

#Data processing
library(CATALYST)
library(scuttle)
library(scater)
library(imcRtools)

#Data visualization
library(cytomapper)
library(dittoSeq)
library(viridis)

#Utilities
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(stringr)
library(BiocParallel)
```

## Read in single-cell information from TMA-based TNBC study
based on [SingleCellExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SingleCellExperiment.html)
class (or [SpatialExperiment]())

### steinbock generated data
The `read_steinbock` function provided by `imcRtools` can now be used to read in
`steinbock` generated data. 

```{r read and inspect steinbock}
sce <- read_steinbock("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/",intensities_folder = "intensities",regionprops_folder = "regionprops", graphs_folder = "neighbors",return_as = "sce")
sce
```

## Single-cell processing

We can set the `colnames` of the object to generate unique identifiers per cell and also set `rownames` to a clean target name.

```{r set-colnames}
colnames(colData(sce))
colnames(sce) <- sce$cell_id <- paste0(sce$sample_id, "_", sce$ObjectNumber)
rownames(sce) <- rowData(sce)$clean_target
```

It is also often the case that sample-specific metadata are available externally. This metadata is available as external excel file:

```{r add metadata, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#read in patient and image metadata
patient_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/data/Metadata_combined_RCC.csv")

images_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/images.csv",col_names = TRUE)
images_meta$names <- str_split(images_meta$image,".tiff",simplify = TRUE)[,1]
images_meta$TMA_id <- str_split(images_meta$acquisition_description," ",simplify = TRUE)[,1]

patient_meta$sample_id <- images_meta$names[match(patient_meta$TMA_id,images_meta$TMA_id)]

#Add metadata to sce
sce$age <- patient_meta$age[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$age_bin <- patient_meta$age_bin[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$gender <- patient_meta$gender[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$type <- patient_meta$type[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$subtype <- patient_meta$subtype[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$ISUP <- patient_meta$ISUP[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$pT_simple <- patient_meta$pT_simple[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$necrose <- patient_meta$necrose[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
sce$lymphocytes <- patient_meta$lymphocytes[match(sce$sample_id,patient_meta$sample_id)]
```


**Transform counts**

Problem: Right-skewed distribution (bias from highly expressing cells)
Solution: Count transformation using an inverse hyperbolic sine function (arcsinh; common in flow cytometry) = leads to linear-like scale near zero and log-like scale beyond a threshold (`cofactor`)
We apply a `cofactor` of `1`. 

```{r transform-counts, message=FALSE}
#Select 5 samples
id <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame %>% select(sample_id) %>% unique %>% slice(1:5) %>% pull(sample_id)

#Raw counts
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD3", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "counts")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD45RA", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "counts")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD68", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "counts")


#Transformed counts
assay(sce, "exprs") <- asinh(counts(sce)/1)

dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD3", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "exprs")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD45RA", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "exprs")
dittoRidgePlot(sce[,sce$sample_id %in% id], var = "CD68", group.by = "sample_id", assay = "exprs")
```

**Define interesting channels**

Subset markers of interest for downstream analysis.

```{r select-features}
rowData(sce)$use_channel <- !grepl("DNA|H3", rowData(sce)$clean_target)
```


## Save single cell object for downstream analysis

Note that masks and images were loaded, modified and saved in the [00_seg_mesmer_QC.Rmd]() script. 

```{r save-objects-read-data}
saveRDS(sce, "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/sce_panimmune_RCC_01.rds")
```
